title: Judah Offers Himself for Benjamin
overview: Joseph, still unrecognized as governor of Egypt, sets a final test to see whether his brothers will abandon their youngest brother Benjamin the way they once abandoned him.

parts.label: The planted cup (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Joseph has his own silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack so Benjamin will look like a thief. Benjamin is the only other son of Joseph's mother Rachel, so the brothers now face the same choice they faced with Joseph years before.

parts.label: Chased and searched (vv. 3-13)
parts.note: The steward says the cup is used for divination, meaning reading signs of the future, a known practice in Egypt; it is unclear whether Joseph really did this or simply used the reputation as part of his act. Tearing their clothes was a traditional sign of grief, and all the brothers going back together shows they will not leave Benjamin.

parts.label: Judah admits guilt (vv. 14-17)
parts.note: When Judah says God has uncovered their guilt, he likely means their old crime of selling Joseph, not stealing the cup. Joseph then offers the others an easy way out: leave Benjamin as a slave and go home free.

parts.label: Judah retells the story (vv. 18-29)
parts.note: Judah speaks with great respect and explains how their aging father already lost one beloved son and could not survive losing Benjamin too. He still repeats the story that Joseph is dead, not knowing he is speaking to Joseph himself.

parts.label: Judah takes his place (vv. 30-34)
parts.note: Judah, who once suggested selling Joseph, now offers to become a slave so Benjamin can go home, showing the brothers have changed. Christians have often read this as a picture of Jesus, a descendant of Judah, taking someone else's place.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether Joseph's harsh test was a purely wise and loving way to discover whether his brothers had changed, or whether it also carried some of his own unhealed hurt.
think: Judah once helped get rid of one brother and now offers his own freedom for another; what do you think it takes for a person to genuinely change?
